data.text: Plan: inspect and group the existing DRC failures plus placement, pad overrides, nets, and antenna keepout; then minimally correct shared board/root causes, place by the documented edge/proximity/keepout rules with rotated dimensions accounted for, route all nets, and document candid draft quality. Files at risk are the PCB, LAYOUT.md, CHANGELOG.md, and DECISIONS.md; key constraints are the 30 × 20 mm maximum, two-layer stackup, 50 Ω RF feed, antenna keepout, and complete connectivity.

args.why: Create the first rule-driven physical layout, eliminate all unrouted electrical connections, and explicitly record which draft-quality aspects remain for specialist review while preserving the documented mechanical, stackup, RF, power, and antenna constraints.
args.what_changes:
- Group the baseline DRC violations by repeated root cause and repair shared causes first.
- Place connectors on board edges, decoupling at U1 supply pins, requested connector protection at connectors if present in the design, and RF parts within the antenna keepout rules.
- Rotate long footprints onto a board axis only where their rotated bounding dimensions fit.
- Preserve B1 manufacturer pad mapping and route every electrical net on the two-layer board, prioritizing zero unconnected items before non-blocking clearance cleanup.
- Add an exact `## Draft quality` section to `docs/LAYOUT.md` listing acceptable draft work and work requiring human or specialist-tool redo.
- Record the layout decisions and append the run to the changelog.
args.tasks:
- [ ] Inspect baseline DRC and group violations by type/root cause.
- [ ] Inspect current placement, net assignments, B1 pad overrides, outline, and antenna keepout.
- [ ] Fix shared/root causes and enforce edge, decoupling, protection, orientation, outline, and keepout placement contracts.
- [ ] Route every electrical net; rerun DRC after small connectivity batches until zero unconnected items, then reconcile remaining blocking violations.
- [ ] Write `docs/LAYOUT.md` Draft quality acceptable/redo items.
- [ ] Update decisions and changelog, check documentation drift, and finish only after DRC passes.

data.name: propose_change

args.why: Create the first rule-driven physical layout, eliminate all unrouted electrical connections, and explicitly record which draft-quality aspects remain for specialist review while preserving the documented mechanical, stackup, RF, power, and antenna constraints.
args.what_changes:
- Group the baseline DRC violations by repeated root cause and repair shared causes first.
- Place connectors on board edges, decoupling at U1 supply pins, requested connector protection at connectors if present in the design, and RF parts within the antenna keepout rules.
- Rotate long footprints onto a board axis only where their rotated bounding dimensions fit.
- Preserve B1 manufacturer pad mapping and route every electrical net on the two-layer board, prioritizing zero unconnected items before non-blocking clearance cleanup.
- Add an exact `## Draft quality` section to `docs/LAYOUT.md` listing acceptable draft work and work requiring human or specialist-tool redo.
- Record the layout decisions and append the run to the changelog.
args.tasks:
- [ ] Inspect baseline DRC and group violations by type/root cause.
- [ ] Inspect current placement, net assignments, B1 pad overrides, outline, and antenna keepout.
- [ ] Fix shared/root causes and enforce edge, decoupling, protection, orientation, outline, and keepout placement contracts.
- [ ] Route every electrical net; rerun DRC after small connectivity batches until zero unconnected items, then reconcile remaining blocking violations.
- [ ] Write `docs/LAYOUT.md` Draft quality acceptable/redo items.
- [ ] Update decisions and changelog, check documentation drift, and finish only after DRC passes.

data.result: proposal written to openspec/changes/layout-draft/ — now call validate_change

data.name: validate_change
data.result: validation passed; edit tools are now unlocked

data.text: Baseline is 77 violations, dominated by 64 missing connections; the shared placement root cause is that all footprints/tracks are near the origin while the 30 × 20 mm outline is at (100,100)–(130,120). J1’s unrotated 23.86 mm courtyard also cannot fit the 20 mm board height. Before the first surgical edit, inspect the existing routing tail and exact coordinate anchors so the layout can be translated/repacked without regenerating the board.

data.text: Placement is now inside the outline, but DRC shows four repeated physical root causes: oversized test-point courtyards intersecting the header/RF chain, C11/C12 too close to U1, crystal capacitors colliding with Y1, and B1’s manufacturer pad pitch below the global clearance. Clear those before adding copper, and create the required candid draft-quality record now.

args.content:
# Layout

The first-draft board uses a 30 mm × 20 mm, two-layer outline. J1 is rotated onto the long board axis at the lower edge; U1 and its supply, crystal, and RF support parts are grouped centrally; the RF chain runs toward AE1 at the right edge. Connector ESD protection remains intentionally absent because `docs/SPEC.md` explicitly excludes it for this short-jumper prototype.

## Draft quality

Fine for a first draft: the board outline remains within 30 mm × 20 mm; J1 is edge-accessible and rotated so its 23.86 mm courtyard fits the 30 mm axis; decoupling and the crystal network are grouped at U1; B1 retains the documented manufacturer pad mapping; AE1 is on the board edge; and the two-layer constraint is preserved.

Redo before release: a human RF specialist must replace the draft RF geometry with a fabricator-stackup-derived 50-ohm feed, validate the Johanson antenna land pattern and keepout against the current datasheet, tune C9/C10/L1/L2 from RF measurements, review return-current continuity and via stitching, refine silkscreen, and verify every courtyard and assembly clearance. Connector ESD remains out of scope unless the prototype cable environment changes.

args.decision: Use the existing 30 mm × 20 mm two-layer outline, rotate J1 onto the 30 mm axis, keep decoupling/crystal parts adjacent to U1, preserve B1 manufacturer pad mapping, and place AE1 at the board edge; retain the documented connector-ESD exclusion.
args.rationale: This is the smallest placement that satisfies the mechanical and functional draft contracts without adding unrequested circuitry, while explicitly deferring RF optimization to stackup-aware specialist review.
args.affects: PCB placement; J1, U1, C1-C12, FB1, Y1, B1, L1-L2, AE1, TP1-TP5; docs/LAYOUT.md
